v.rationale: All three use the same design: an invokable controller, a FormRequest `after()` hook for business-rule 422s, an enum cast and an invokable pricing class. All test suites pass. impl-2 ranks first. It has the most idiomatic Collection use in pricing, no bugs turned up in my probes, and the broadest tests, including the empty cart, rounding and leftover cents. impl-3 is nearly identical but slightly less idiomatic: it passes arrays around and uses an assignment inside a condition. It also hardcodes DKK via Number::currency in a cents-only API, and its tests are slightly narrower. impl-1 adds useful features (case and whitespace normalisation, rejecting category codes that match nothing), but probes found real bugs. An empty cart gets a garbled 'only applies to items in the  category' error. Any code stored in lowercase can never be redeemed, because only the input is uppercased. Its pricing class also falls back to raw array_* functions instead of Collections.
